title: Mother Superior EA just had its best live week so far
author: Livid_Parsnip_2816
selftext:
**Mother Superior EA just had its best live week so far**

Four months of building and testing, and it’s nice to finally see her trading live.

This week finished at **+7.74%**, bringing October to **+21.46%**. The screenshot shows the daily breakdown, including the days without trades.

Mother Superior is my multi-strategy gold EA for MT5. It uses a recovery layer, so the closed results are only part of the picture — floating drawdown and combined exposure matter too. The live history is still short, but I’m pleased with the start.

Disclosure: I’m the developer, and the EA is available commercially.

[https://www.mql5.com/en/market/product/183855](https://www.mql5.com/en/market/product/183855)

comments.author: SPXQuantAlgo
comments.body: If it worked you would use it yourself instead of selling it and letting the “edge” evaporate

replies.author: Livid_Parsnip_2816
replies.body: The edge will be just fine, and if someone isn't a millionaire, they don't even have the basic capital to trade.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: with a recovery layer the closed results don't say much on their own, the floating drawdown is what shows how close the account got to the wall. a week where the recovery leg rescued a loser looks exactly like a clean week in closed P&L.

replies.author: Livid_Parsnip_2816
replies.body: So far, the DD has been at most 15%; I've developed a really good recovery system.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: 15% on closed trades or on floating? with a recovery layer those two can sit very far apart, and the floating one is what the broker looks at when margin gets tight.

replies.author: Livid_Parsnip_2816
replies.body: The 15% was floating equity drawdown across all open positions. In that recovery sequence, gold moved roughly $120 against the initial entry before the first additional DCA trade was opened.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: $120 against before the first add is a wide first step on gold, so most of that 15% came from the original entry on its own. that's the better version of the story, the adds weren't what stacked it.

replies.author: Livid_Parsnip_2816
replies.body: Yeah, that’s fair. The first add was roughly $120 away, so most of the 15% floating DD came from the original position. The recovery didn’t keep stacking trades as gold moved against it. But 15% floating DD is still something I have to watch closely.
